source: inputs/plain-spec.md of the coherence study, decomposed into atomic rules by Claude on 2026-10-07. Applied identically to every write-up in both arms.
instruction_to_extractor: For each rule, answer recoverable=true only if a reader holding ONLY the write-up could state this rule correctly, and quote the words that carry it. If the write-up is silent, ambiguous, or says something else, answer false and quote the closest text or write absent.

rules.rule: There are exactly six positions in a line, numbered 1 to 6, with a stated direction.
Each position holds a whole-number quantity that is never negative.
Each position has a fixed capacity: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7.
Each position has an upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5.
Each position has a lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2.
Starting quantities are 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1, and all positions start in the resting state.
The global limit is 38 and the loss tally starts at 0.
There are exactly five cycles, and the input table gives one row of six amounts per cycle: (0,6,3,5,3,3), (4,2,0,1,1,7), (4,4,3,0,0,6), (7,6,7,1,3,0), (0,6,6,3,3,0).
Each cycle has five steps in a fixed order, and each step finishes for all positions before the next step starts.
Step 1 adds the cycle's input to each position, and capacity is not enforced in this step.
Step 2 handles positions one at a time in order 1 to 6; a position over capacity passes its excess to the next position and is set to exactly its capacity.
In step 2, excess passed to the next position counts before that position is handled, so overflow can cascade within the same step.
In step 2, excess from position 6 goes to the loss tally.
Step 3 reads the quantity after step 2: a resting position at or above its upper mark becomes raised.
In step 3, a raised position at or below its lower mark becomes resting.
In step 3, a position strictly between the marks keeps its state, and a position changes at most once per cycle.
Step 4 computes all six amounts first, from the quantities at the start of the step and the states set in step 3, before any amount is applied.
In step 4, a resting position releases floor(quantity / 4), and the amount goes to the loss tally.
In step 4, a raised position releases floor(quantity / 2), and the amount goes to the previous position (n-1); position 1's raised release goes to the loss tally.
In step 4, every position loses its own release amount, and capacity is not enforced; a position may end over capacity, corrected only at the next cycle's step 2, and never after cycle 5.
Step 5 fires only when the total of the six quantities is strictly greater than 38; a total of exactly 38 does nothing.
When step 5 fires, each position becomes floor(quantity / 2), the removed amount from each position goes to the loss tally, and the cycle is recorded.

The report lists the six end quantities, the six end states, every state change as (cycle, position, before, after), the cycles in which step 5 fired, the loss tally, and a balance check: start total plus all inputs equals end total plus the loss tally.
